To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the degree of left ventricular diasterolic impairment and left ventricular remodeling is associated with the intensity of cardiovascular disease risk factor therapy in patients with coronary artery disease.

in patients with multiple risk factors for cardiovascular disease, the adequacy of medical treatment for these factors is associated with improved left ventricular diastsolic properties and remodeling, even when patients are not hypertensive.
the number of CAD or CVDRFs and ‘intensity’ of medication therapy are not associated with LV diastolic properties or remodeling in patients without overt LV dysfunction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of medical therapy for CAD/CVRFs on left ventricular remodeling and diastole in patients with normal systolic function.
the impact of medication therapy for cardiovascular disease (CVD) on the diastolic properties of the left ventricle (LV).
the effects of medication on diastolic function in a cohort of patients with multiple CAD/CVDRF.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adequate medication therapy for underlying cardiovascular risk factors is associated with better left ventricular diastic properties.
in patients with preserved systolic function, the number of CVDRFs is not a predictor of LV diastole dysfunction, while the intensity of therapy is a predictor.
in patients with preserved left ventricular (LV), systolic function and normal LV geometry, the number of CAD and CVDRFs was not associated with differences in diastolic properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the degree of LV remodeling and diastole function are associated with the degree of medication therapy for underlying cardiovascular disease and cardiovascular disease risk factors.

in patients with normal LV systolic function, the number of CAD and CVDRFs is not associated with LV diastolic dysfunction, but the adequacy of treatment for these conditions is associated with LV dias-tolic dysfunction and remodeling.

in patients with multiple cardiovascular risk factors, the adequacy of treatment with medication therapy may play a role in determining the severity of diastolic dysfunction and left ventricular remodeling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of CAD or CVDRFs does not necessarily predict diastolic dysfunction or LV remodeling, but that the adequacy of therapy for each identified risk factor does.
adequate treatment of cardiovascular risk factors is associated with less left ventricular remodeling and diastole dysfunction.
patients with multiple CVRFs may benefit from more aggressive medical therapy.
